figures.title: Monohybrid Cross — Mendel's Experiment
whatItShows: Cross between TT (tall) × tt (dwarf) pea plants
F1: all Tt (tall) — dominance of T over t
F2 selfing gives 3 Tall : 1 Dwarf (3:1 phenotypic ratio)
Genotypic ratio: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt
figures.neetTip: NEET asks: What is the phenotypic ratio in F2 of a monohybrid cross? Answer: 3:1. Genotypic: 1:2:1. Don't confuse the two!

figures.title: Dihybrid Cross — 9:3:3:1 Ratio
whatItShows: RRYY (round yellow) × rryy (wrinkled green)
F1: all RrYy — Round Yellow (both dominant)
F2: 9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green
Proves genes on different chromosomes assort independently
figures.neetTip: When ratio deviates from 9:3:3:1 it indicates epistasis. Know all epistatic ratios: 9:7 (complementary), 12:3:1 (dominant epistasis), 9:3:4 (recessive epistasis).

figures.title: Pedigree Chart Symbols & Analysis
whatItShows: Square = Male, Circle = Female
Filled = Affected, Half-filled = Carrier
Horizontal line = Mating, Vertical line = Offspring
Used to determine autosomal/X-linked dominant/recessive inheritance
figures.neetTip: If ALL sons of an affected father are normal → X-linked. If father affected and daughter affected → Autosomal dominant. Two normal parents → Affected child = Autosomal recessive.
figures.memoryAid: Father→Son via Y: no X-linked trait passes father to son directly

figures.title: DNA Double Helix — Watson & Crick Model
whatItShows: Two antiparallel strands — one 3'→5', other 5'→3'
Base pairing: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)
Diameter: 2 nm | Pitch: 3.4 nm | Base pairs per turn: 10
Sugar-phosphate backbone on outside, bases inside
figures.neetTip: Frequently asked: 'If A=30% then G=?' — Use Chargaff's rule: A=T, G=C, A+G=50%. So G=C=20%. Also: G+C content determines DNA stability.
figures.memoryAid: AT = 2 bonds (weak) | GC = 3 bonds (strong) → GC-rich DNA is more stable

figures.title: Meselson & Stahl Experiment
whatItShows: E. coli grown in ¹⁵N (heavy) medium → all ¹⁵N DNA
Transferred to ¹⁴N medium → after 1 division: hybrid ¹⁴N/¹⁵N
After 2 divisions: 50% hybrid + 50% light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N)
Proved Semi-conservative replication — each strand serves as template
figures.neetTip: NEET asks which type of replication was proved — always Semi-conservative. Taylor et al proved it in Vicia faba (plant). Kornberg enzyme = DNA Pol III in prokaryotes.
figures.memoryAid: Semi-conservative = half old, half new in EACH daughter DNA

figures.title: Lac Operon — Jacob & Monod Model
whatItShows: Structural genes: lacZ (β-galactosidase), lacY (permease), lacA (transacetylase)
Regulator gene → Repressor protein binds operator → blocks transcription
Lactose (inducer) → binds repressor → releases operator → genes ON
Glucose present: cAMP low → CAP inactive → transcription low (catabolite repression)
figures.neetTip: Most tested: Which enzyme breaks lactose? β-galactosidase (lacZ). Lac operon is INDUCIBLE. Trp operon is REPRESSIBLE. Glucose = catabolite repression via cAMP-CAP.
figures.memoryAid: Lactose = Inducer → Repressor OFF → Genes ON (like a switch)

figures.title: Transcription — DNA to mRNA
whatItShows: Template strand (antisense 3'→5') is read by RNA Polymerase
mRNA synthesised 5'→3' direction
Prokaryotes: no nuclear membrane, translation begins before transcription ends
Eukaryotes: hnRNA → capping + polyadenylation + splicing → mRNA
figures.neetTip: NEET asks: Which strand is template? The one read 3'→5'. Coding strand = non-template strand = same sequence as mRNA (but T→U). RNA Pol needs no primer.
figures.memoryAid: Template = antisense = non-coding. Coding strand = sense strand = same as mRNA

figures.title: Translation — mRNA to Protein
whatItShows: Ribosome moves 5'→3' on mRNA
A site: aminoacyl-tRNA enters | P site: peptide bond forms | E site: empty tRNA exits
Start codon: AUG (Met) | Stop codons: UAA, UAG, UGA
Polysomes: multiple ribosomes on one mRNA simultaneously
figures.neetTip: Stop codons: UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber), UGA (Opal/Umber) — no tRNA for these. AUG also codes for fMet in prokaryotes. Shine-Dalgarno sequence for ribosome binding in prokaryotes.
figures.memoryAid: Stop codons: UAA, UAG, UGA = 'U Are Away', 'U Are Gone', 'U Go Away'
